raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Blocked on https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5799

With expandable_segments enabled, hipIpcGetMemHandle cannot export the VMM-backed pointers the caching allocator hands out, so AITER's custom all-reduce falls back to staging every input through a device-to-device copy. On an 8x MI355X Kimi-K3 decode that is one copyBuffer per all-reduce, 1160 of 1160 launches across all ranks, ~1.2 ms per forward pass.

The activations feeding those all-reduces are allocated inside CUDA graph capture from the graph's private pool, so disabling expandable segments for the duration of capture is enough to make them IPC-exportable and let AITER take its registered path. Weights, KV cache and eager allocations keep expandable segments.

Off by default behind VLLM_NON_EXPANDABLE_CUDAGRAPH_POOL. The toggle follows CuMemAllocator.use_memory_pool, which flips the same allocator setting around the sleep-mode pool.

+class _FakeAllocator:
+    """Stands in for the torch allocator: records writes, reports live state."""

+    def __init__(self, conf: str, honours_writes: bool = True, readable: bool = True):

+def test_guard_toggles_off_and_restores(fake):
+    alloc = fake("expandable_segments:True")

+        assert applied is True
+        assert alloc.read() is False, "body must run with expandable segments off"

+    reformatting cannot break it.

+    import inspect

+    src = inspect.getsource(parallel_state.graph_capture)
+    fn = ast.parse(inspect.cleandoc(src)).body[0]
+    with_stmts = [n for n in ast.walk(fn) if isinstance(n, ast.With)]
+    assert with_stmts, "graph_capture should use a with statement"
+    calls = [ast.unparse(item.context_expr) for item in with_stmts[0].items]
+    guard_at = next(
+        (i for i, c in enumerate(calls) if "non_expandable_allocations" in c), None
+    )
+    assert guard_at is not None, calls
+    tp_at = next((i for i, c in enumerate(calls) if "get_tp_group" in c), None)

+@contextmanager
+def non_expandable_allocations(enabled: bool = True) -> Generator[bool, None, None]:
+    """Run the body with ``expandable_segments`` off, then restore the config.
+
+    Yields whether the toggle was actually applied. Re-entrant: only the
+    outermost context writes to the allocator. The restore is unconditional --
+    a stale or unavailable reader costs a log line, never allocator state.
+    """
+    global _non_expandable_depth
+    if not enabled or _non_expandable_depth > 0:
+        yield False
+        return

+    prev_conf = current_alloc_conf()
+    live = expandable_segments_enabled()

+    )
+    if not was_enabled:
+        yield False
+        return
+
+    _non_expandable_depth += 1
+    prev_env = {n: os.environ[n] for n in ALLOC_CONF_ENV_VARS if n in os.environ}
+    try:
+        try:
+            set_alloc_conf(with_conf_flag(prev_conf, EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS, False))
+            for name, value in prev_env.items():
+                os.environ[name] = with_conf_flag(value, EXPANDABLE_SEGMENTS, False)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            logger.warning(
+                "Could not disable expandable_segments (%s); "
+                "leaving the allocator alone.",

+            )
+            yield False
+            return
+
+        if expandable_segments_enabled():
+            logger.warning(
+                "Requested non-expandable allocations, but the allocator still "
+                "reports expandable_segments=True; allocations made here may "
+                "stay VMM-backed and non-IPC-exportable."
+            )
+            yield False
+            return
+
+        logger.info(
+            "Disabled expandable_segments so that allocations made here stay "
+            "IPC-exportable; the previous allocator config is restored on exit."
+        )
+        yield True
+    finally:
+        _non_expandable_depth -= 1
+        for name, value in prev_env.items():
+            os.environ[name] = value
+        try:
+            set_alloc_conf(prev_conf)
+        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
+            logger.warning("Could not restore the allocator config: %s", exc)
